text:
sam: Heads up — saw steady mem growth on the KV cache for long-lived sessions. Reuse hits are high but heap + fragmentation climbs over hours.
maria: Can you paste the metric slice and a repro? which deployment (hosted/dedicated)?
sam: Dedicated pool-id=dp-17. Observed after ~6k requests from same session id, rss: 1.1GB -> 3.3GB. eviction_count low, page_faults spike. Example logs:
```
[2026-03-15 09:12:01] kv: insert key=conv:abc123:prefix:token-0 size=24B
[2026-03-15 11:14:33] kv: reuse hit=conv:abc123:prefix:token-0
[2026-03-15 11:14:33] mem: rss=3321MB frag=28% evictions=12
```
lee: Hmm looks like keyspace sparsity + small-value churn. If keys include ephemeral session nonce we end up with many tiny allocations and fragmented arena.
olivia: Can we normalize keys to drop short-lived nonce, and add per-session TTL + compaction pass? That should collapse fragmentation.
rex: Two quick ideas: 1) shard keys by hash -> reduces lock contention and buckets arena, 2) use expiry buckets and background compaction to coalesce free lists.
maria: Also want to rule out kernel-level allocator issues. Can you run jemalloc stats and heap profile across timeframe? If kernel selection influences perf, we should test both default and tcmalloc/jemalloc from perf images.
sam: Ran jemalloc: fragmentation still present but different numbers (frag 18% vs 28%), same overall growth. Batching heuristics may exacerbate prefix reuse — larger batches cause longer-lived KV entries (prefetched prefixes) to stay hot.
lee: Short-term mitigation: enforce prefix-key canonicalization and add a sticky-session policy toggle (sticky=true -> reuse same cache shard, sticky=false -> per-request ephemeral entries). We can A/B test sticky toggle.
olivia: Suggested key canonicalization (pseudo):
```
string canonical_key(string prefix, string session_id) {
  // drop ephemeral nonce parts
  auto norm = regex_replace(prefix, r"-nonce:[0-9a-f]{8}", "");
  return hash64(norm) + ":s=" + (sticky ? session_id : "g");
}
```
maria: +1 to runtime flag. Also add metrics: cache_hit_by_shard, avg_entry_lifetime, compaction_runs.
rex: For rollout: small % of dedicated hosts with compaction enabled and normalized keys, measure rss, frag, evictions, tail latency. If mem drops >25% and latency stable -> roll.
sam: I'll spin up an experiment today. Will attach heap snapshots and jemalloc output when available.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: kv-key-normalize-experiment -> canary on dp-17 at 2026-03-16T02:00Z :rocket:
olivia: Great, also let's instrument a kernel-selection matrix: run on cpu-bound vs nvlink configs to ensure no regression from allocator interplay with contended kernels.
lee: Filed followups: add TTL per-prefix, compaction throttle, and an observability dashboard tile for 'kv fragmentation' -> @maria please own the dashboard.
maria: On it. I'll create a dashboard and a perf playbook for when frag > 20%.
sam: Thanks everyone — will post results in this thread. :eyes:
